terms.comment: “A part of the world”, Traupman’s first choice. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

terms.gloss: a continent, a part of the world
terms.comment: Traupman warns against continēns, which classically means the mainland as against islands. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase. Pliny has nūllā in parte mundī, “in no part of the world” (Lewis & Short s.v. mundus), but not of a continent.
Classically the mainland, as against islands (see mainland); its use for one of the continents is modern.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
